We intend to accelerate shareholder returns and increase shareholder value by controlling operating costs and capital expenditures, maximizing reserve recoveries and making disciplined strategic accretive acquisitions that meet our strategic and financial objectives.
Over the past several years, we have delivered on our focused strategy and believe we will continue to do so with the organic growth programs across our diversified portfolio over the coming years.

Our future success in growing proved reserves, production and balancing the long-term development of our assets with a focus on generating attractive corporate-level returns will be highly dependent on the capital resources available to us.
In the event additional capital is needed, we may not be able to obtain debt or equity financing on terms favorable to us, on expected timelines, or at all.

If aggregate borrowings exceed 35% of specified thresholds, our 2025 RBL Facility requires us to enter into commodity price hedge positions establishing certain minimum fixed prices for anticipated future production.

Our material cash requirements generally consist of capital projects, finance and operating leases, dividend payments, Merged Concession Agreement and abandonment funding, each of which is discussed in further detail below.

Capital Projects and Expenditures - For the nine months ended September 30, 2026, we had accrual basis capital expenditures of $256.3 million compared to $147.6 million of accrual basis capital expenditures for the same period in 2025.
See “Recent Operational Updates” above for additional information regarding our capital projects.
Dividend Policy - Our Board of Directors adopted a quarterly cash dividend policy of an expected $0.0625 per common share per quarter, which commenced in the first quarter of 2023.

We recorded a $108.9 million net loss on derivative instruments for the nine months ended September 30, 2026, which included an unrealized loss of $46.9 million related to the change in fair value of our commodity derivative contracts primarily driven by an increase in the futures curve for forecasted commodity prices and a realized loss of $61.9 million on matured commodity derivative contracts.

estimates.t: There have been no material changes to our critical accounting policies and estimates subsequent to December 31, 2025.

statements.t: Additionally, the Company provided operational and financial guidance for the fourth quarter and full year of 2026.

George Maxwell, Vaalco’s Chief Executive Officer, commented, “The third quarter results continue to demonstrate our ability to successfully execute on our strategy as we deliver on our forecasts and grow production in a strong commodity price environment.
In Q3 2026, we had strong sales volumes, toward the high end of our guidance, with production up 21% compared to Q2 2026 and continued increased realized pricing.
We will have an active drilling program in Côte d’Ivoire and Egypt in 2027 that should continue to grow our production.

We remain confident in our strategic vision with continued operational success and preparing for our next major programs at Venus in Equatorial Guinea and Kossipo in Côte d’Ivoire, which should organically double the Company’s production.

Subject to such approval and entry into the second exploration phase, the Company will be required under the CI-705 PSC to relinquish approximately 25% of the Phase 1 Block CI-705 area and undertake certain minimum work and investment obligations, including the reprocessing of 3D seismic data, geological and geophysical studies, and the drilling of one firm exploration well.
The Company continued to hedge a portion of its expected future production to protect cash flow generation to assist in funding its capital and shareholder return programs.
The Company has provided fourth quarter 2026 guidance and its full year 2026 guidance.
